samples.summary: Cmd+\ (clear formatting) and Cmd+Alt+V (format painter) bypass the new cell-rectangle route and clear/restyle the ENTIRE table when a cell rectangle is selected
samples.evidence:
The change makes `Doc.applyInlineStyle` explicitly ignore `range.tableCellRange` ("the editors route a cell rectangle to `applyStyleToCellRange` above this call", document.ts:357) and adds `applyInlineStyleToCells` for that shape. `TextEditor.toggleStyle` (text-editor.ts:2924) and `editor.ts` `applyStyleImpl` (editor.ts:1043) do route rectangles, but two other writers do not:

- `TextEditor.clearFormatting` — `this.doc.applyInlineStyle(range, clearStyle)` (text-editor.ts:2862) with no `range.tableCellRange` check.
- Format-painter apply — `this.doc.applyInlineStyle(this.selection.range, this.styleBuffer)` (text-editor.ts:1010), same omission.

For a multi-cell rectangle the anchor and focus live in different cells, so `visitRangeSlices` falls to the top-level branch (range-slices.ts:149-155): both endpoints normalize to the *same* parent table block, `fromIdx === toIdx`, and the table branch at range-slices.ts:168-176 visits every block of every cell. Result: Cmd+\ over a 2×2 selection in a 10×10 table strips inline formatting from all 100 cells, and format painter repaints all of them. This is destructive to user formatting outside the selection. (The behaviour predates the diff, but the diff is exactly what establishes `applyInlineStyleToCells` as the required route and leaves these two call sites unconverted.)

samples.summary: Toolbar style write on a body↔table-cell range marks only the parent table dirty, leaving the styled body blocks rendered from a stale layout cache
samples.evidence: `applyStyleImpl` writes the whole range via `doc.applyInlineStyle(range, style)` (editor.ts:1051) — which, after this change, is also the traversal the summary reports, so a body-to-cell selection is now a first-class, reachable case (the new test `cell endpoints normalize to the parent table` at test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts asserts exactly this shape). But the dirty marking that follows is exclusive: `if (anchorCI) markDirty(anchorCI.tableBlockId); else if (focusCI) ... else { mark the body index span }` (editor.ts:1053-1070). When one endpoint is a cell block, only the table block is marked; the top-level body blocks that `applyInlineStyle` just restyled are never marked, so `computeLayout(..., dirtyBlockIds, layoutCache, ...)` reuses their cached lines and the new style is not painted until an unrelated edit invalidates them.

samples.summary: `visitCellRectangleSlices` uses the raw cell rectangle while the painted selection expands it for merged cells, so highlighted merged cells can be neither read nor written
samples.evidence: `visitCellRectangleSlices` clamps `cellRange.start/end` to the table dimensions but never expands for merges (range-slices.ts:53-59), whereas the selection rendering normalizes through `expandCellRangeForMerges` (view/selection.ts:100-113, 56-98), which grows the rectangle so every merged cell it touches is fully contained. A merged cell whose top-left sits outside the raw rectangle is therefore painted as selected but skipped by both the summary read and `Doc.applyInlineStyleToCells`' write (`if (!cell || cell.colSpan === 0) continue`, range-slices.ts:63) — the user sees a highlighted cell that Bold does not change. Read and write agree with each other, but both disagree with what the user sees selected.

samples.summary: A text (non-rectangle) selection spanning two cells of one table silently styles the whole table, and the summary now reports the whole table too
samples.evidence: In the top-level branch, two endpoints in different cells of the same table both normalize to that table's index, so `fromIdx === toIdx` and the loop body takes the `block.type === 'table'` path (range-slices.ts:164-177), covering every block of every cell whole — the partial offsets `from.offset`/`to.offset` are discarded. Selecting a couple of words across a cell boundary and pressing Cmd+B therefore bolds the entire table. The write behaved this way before, but the read did not (it returned an empty summary), so the diff makes the toolbar actively report 'the whole table is bold' and the toggle a whole-table operation. Worth confirming this is intended rather than an artefact of unifying the two walks.

finding.summary: Cmd+\ (clear formatting) and Cmd+Alt+V (format painter) bypass the new cell-rectangle route and clear/restyle the ENTIRE table when a cell rectangle is selected
finding.evidence:
The change makes `Doc.applyInlineStyle` explicitly ignore `range.tableCellRange` ("the editors route a cell rectangle to `applyStyleToCellRange` above this call", document.ts:357) and adds `applyInlineStyleToCells` for that shape. `TextEditor.toggleStyle` (text-editor.ts:2924) and `editor.ts` `applyStyleImpl` (editor.ts:1043) do route rectangles, but two other writers do not:

- `TextEditor.clearFormatting` — `this.doc.applyInlineStyle(range, clearStyle)` (text-editor.ts:2862) with no `range.tableCellRange` check.
- Format-painter apply — `this.doc.applyInlineStyle(this.selection.range, this.styleBuffer)` (text-editor.ts:1010), same omission.

For a multi-cell rectangle the anchor and focus live in different cells, so `visitRangeSlices` falls to the top-level branch (range-slices.ts:149-155): both endpoints normalize to the *same* parent table block, `fromIdx === toIdx`, and the table branch at range-slices.ts:168-176 visits every block of every cell. Result: Cmd+\ over a 2×2 selection in a 10×10 table strips inline formatting from all 100 cells, and format painter repaints all of them. This is destructive to user formatting outside the selection. (The behaviour predates the diff, but the diff is exactly what establishes `applyInlineStyleToCells` as the required route and leaves these two call sites unconverted.)

verdict.reason: Both unconverted call sites exist exactly as described: clearFormatting calls this.doc.applyInlineStyle(range, clearStyle) at text-editor.ts:2862 with no tableCellRange check (Cmd+\ binding at text-editor.ts:925-929), and the format-painter apply calls this.doc.applyInlineStyle(this.selection.range, this.styleBuffer) at text-editor.ts:1010 guarded only by styleBuffer && hasSelection(). Selection.hasSelection() returns true for a cell rectangle (selection.ts:670), so both paths are reachable with a rectangle selected. Doc.applyInlineStyle (document.ts:360-365) deliberately ignores range.tableCellRange (comment at document.ts:357-358) and delegates to visitRangeSlices. For a multi-cell rectangle the drag code sets anchor in one cell's block and focus in the target cell's first block (text-editor.ts:1799-1802 / 1819-1822), so anchor.blockId !== focus.blockId and the cells differ: visitRangeSlices skips the same-block branch (range-slices.ts:108-115) and the same-cell branch (123-147), reaching the top-level branch (149-155) where both endpoints normalize to the same parent table block and fromIdx === toIdx; the table branch (168-176) then visits every block of every cell. Result: Cmd+\ or format painter over a sub-rectangle rewrites inline styles across the whole table, destroying formatting outside the selection — a data-loss/wrong-behavior bug in the correctness lane. Only toggleStyle (text-editor.ts:2924-2929) and editor.ts:1043-1044 route to the cell-rectangle path.

finding.summary: New read walk guards a negative block index; the matching write path (`Doc.applyInlineStyle`) still does not, so the same range crashes on write
finding.evidence: `visitStyledRunsInRange` (range-runs.ts:159-161) does `const anchorIdx = doc.getBlockIndex(anchorTopId); ... if (anchorIdx < 0 || focusIdx < 0) return;` and also `if (!block) continue;` at line 172. The write path it is explicitly mirroring has neither guard: document.ts:395-411 computes `startBlock`/`endBlock` from `getBlockIndex` (which returns -1 when the normalized top id is not in the current context — e.g. an endpoint inside a *nested* table cell, whose `blockParentMap` entry points at the inner table block that is not a context block, or a cell block whose parent-map entry is missing because layout has not run since the table was inserted), then loops `for (let i = fromBlockIdx; i <= toBlockIdx; i++) { const block = contextBlocks[i]; ... if (block.type === 'table' ...)` — with i === -1 `block` is `undefined` and `block.type` throws a TypeError. Because the toolbar/keyboard now derive an *empty* summary for exactly these ranges (the read returns early), a toggle still calls `applyStyle`/`toggleStyle` on that range and reaches the unguarded write. The read-side guard makes the divergence silent instead of surfacing it.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts the write path `Doc.applyInlineStyle` contains its own unguarded block-index walk (`startBlock`/`endBlock` from `getBlockIndex`, then `for (let i = fromBlockIdx; i <= toBlockIdx; i++) { const block = contextBlocks[i]; ... block.type ... }`) at document.ts:395-411. That code is not present. document.ts:395-411 is `setBlockType`/`deleteBlock`. The real `applyInlineStyle` is document.ts:360-365 and is a three-line delegation to `visitRangeSlices(this, range, ...)` — it contains no `getBlockIndex`, no index loop, and no `contextBlocks` access. The read (`visitStyledRunsInRange`, range-runs.ts:80) drives the exact same `visitRangeSlices`, so the guards the reviewer credits only to the read — `if (anchorIdx < 0 || focusIdx < 0) return;` (range-slices.ts:155) and `if (!block) continue;` (range-slices.ts:166) — are on the shared traversal and protect the write identically. A nested-table or stale-parent-map endpoint therefore returns early on both sides; `contextBlocks[-1].type` is unreachable from the write, so there is no divergence and no TypeError. The finding's quoted evidence is also mislocated: range-runs.ts is only 81 lines and has no line 159-161 and no `getBlockIndex` call; that guard lives in range-slices.ts. I additionally checked the only other `getBlockIndex` uses in document.ts (line 270, guarded by `if (blockIndex <= 0) return pos;` at line 271; line 315, used as `insertBlock(blockIndex + 1, ...)`), neither of which is the styling path described.
